items.summary: Representatives from Nvidia privately told Illinois Representative Bill Foster that implementing the anti-smuggling measures in the Chip Security Act would be technically feasible, even though an industry group publicly called them “potentially infeasible.” The Semiconductor Industry Association explicitly opposed the bill’s tracking mandates as new and untested. Privately, however, Nvidia representatives reportedly responded during technical discussions with Foster that they could implement such safeguards. Other technology Nvidia has built suggests it can track chip locations accurately.
items.title: Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling, even as industry publicly questioned feasibility

items.summary: WIRED explored who the most powerful women in tech are, concluding that Colette Kress—Nvidia's interim CEO and former CFO—is currently its most powerful woman. When asked for his views, Jensen Huang named Meta's Dina Powell and Google's Ruth Porat as he thought of them in Washington, later praising SpaceX's Gwynne Shotwell. Notably, he did not mention Kress, the highest-ranking woman executive at his own company, an omission WIRED framed among a pattern of overlooked women leaders.
items.title: Jensen Huang Omitted Nvidia's Colette Kress from His List of Powerful Women in Tech

items.summary: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned amid revelations of an extramarital affair and a relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese-linked executive suspected by US officials of smuggling chips. Analyst Nils Pratley argues the departure was not scandal-driven but strategically necessary: Nvidia's share price fell 13% initially before recovering to a 5% drop as investors recalled its dominant graphics processing units. The board acted because congressional scrutiny into chip exports would occur regardless, Huang's lobbying credibility had evaporated, and over-reliance on one leader posed governance risks. CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while independent director Harvey Jones takes the chair to address long-dodged governance concerns.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia Exit Was Inevitable Despite 'Irreplaceable' Myth

items.summary: Google launched the elemental-named Gemini 4 Hydrogen, replacing the widely used Gemini 3.8 Flash across its products (s5). Unlike earlier staged rollouts restricted to cybersecurity researchers and top-tier subscribers, access began immediately with relaxed limits (s2-s4). Google claims Hydrogen is 2.5 times faster than Flash 3.8 in high mode (s7), cuts fabricated claims by more than fivefold (s8), triples Terminal-Bench code-generation scores (s9), and scored 54 versus Argon's 50 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with xhigh mode (s11).
items.title: Google Deploys Gemini 4 Hydrogen as Flash Successor

items.summary: Families protested in seven cities nationwide against Google's push to embed its Gemini AI into schools, with no option for students to use Search without AI. In Chicago, ILFPS rallied outside Google's downtown office and demanded an AI moratorium until student risks are understood. The group previously pressured CPS to cancel a districtwide Gemini pilot. If successful, it would join Los Angeles and New York City in cautiously restricting school AI.
items.title: Google Faces Calls for AI Moratoriums After Gemini Pilot Backlash

items.summary: MIT Lincoln Laboratory earned three of the 100 most significant innovations recognized in the 2026 R&D 100 Awards, which honor technologies transitioning to use or licensing since 1963. The winners address cybersecurity, quantum computing, and communications. Magnetite is an inherently secure operating system built on seL4 with Rust services under least-privilege isolation; it was also named the laboratory's Best Invention of 2025. The Quantum Microsystems platform integrates hundreds of superconductor and semiconductor chips into a wafer-scale system using AI-driven routing, digital lithography, and microbump connections to replace bulky coaxial cables. An algorithm cancels interference from 5G base stations on co-channel RF devices such as military radars; validated against signals captured at Hill Air Force Base, it restored a radar signal within two decibels of its original ratio, preserving 89 percent of detection range.
items.title: Three MIT Lincoln Laboratory Technologies Win 2026 R&D 100 Awards

items.summary: Google is improving its search with the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which it calls its biggest search improvement yet. Unlike Carbon and Argon models built for deep reasoning, Hydrogen prioritizes speed across agentic tasks. Google says it runs 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash while still beating Argon on one intelligence benchmark. The update brings better intent understanding, clearer answers, more visual responses, improved fan-out search, and a new xhigh thinking level.
items.title: Google Rolls Out Gemini 4 Hydrogen for Search

items.summary: A widespread Microsoft 365 outage disrupted Outlook, Teams and Copilot globally. Downdetector reported surging complaints Thursday afternoon across services including Azure, OneDrive and the Store. Advisory MO1550821 confirmed failures in Exchange Online, SharePoint Online and Defender XDR. The incident began at 1:26 PM ET after servers unexpectedly became unavailable, straining remaining infrastructure; Microsoft paused deployments and redistributed traffic while restarting affected servers.
items.title: Microsoft 365 Outage Disrupts Outlook, Teams and Copilot Worldwide

items.summary: A widespread Microsoft outage disrupted Outlook, Teams, Copilot, and OneDrive on Thursday morning in the U.S., with Downdetector reporting nearly 83,000 Outlook issues that dropped to under 75,000 by late afternoon. Microsoft attributed the problem not to increased traffic but to servers unexpectedly becoming unavailable and straining remaining infrastructure; it paused deployments while restarting affected systems.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Affects Multiple Services Amid Server Failures

items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia on November 12, following revelations of affairs with two women, one suspected by U.S. intelligence officials of being a Chinese spy. As the world's largest supplier of chips for AI data centers—controlling an estimated 80% of the market and valued at around $5 trillion as of November 3—the company's stock fell to $4 trillion amid the scandal.
items.title: Nvidia's AI Dominance and Jensen Huang's Scandal Fallout

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Google's new Pixel Tag Bluetooth tracker delivers reduced functionality on older Android devices, as its best features require Android 9.0+ and Bluetooth 6.0+. Smartphones began shipping with Bluetooth 6.0 in 2025 starting with the Samsung Galaxy S26 series, while most premium phones also include ultra-wideband chips for short-range precision finding that base models lack. The $30 tracker remains affordable compared to competitors like Tile Tag and Chipolo Loop.
items.title: Google Pixel Tag Tracking Limitations on Older Android Phones

items.summary: AWS released AWS Emulator, a free local emulator serving the AWS API surface without requiring an account or fees. Autonomous agents wrote and reviewed all code under a pipeline combining test writers, issue finders, fixers and security reviewers; humans built tests and merge gates. Built from 438 models across 200+ services, release v1.0.322 passes 56.6% of 42,857 fidelity tests overall (KMS strongest at 93.9%, CloudFormation weakest at 15.8%). It runs on Linux or Docker with a 2 GiB cap and is intended for fast local and CI loops rather than security or load testing.
items.title: AWS Emulator: An AI-Agent-Built Local Copy of AWS APIs

items.summary: Constellation Energy, the nation's largest nuclear fleet operator serving roughly 2.5 million retail customers and capacity equivalent to 27 million homes, faced fragmented data as it grew through acquisitions like Calpine in 2026. A single question—'How many customers do we have?'—yielded three correct answers across billing, wholesale, and CRM systems. To resolve this, Constellation built a governed Enterprise Data Platform on Databricks with Unity Catalog to enforce shared definitions and governance. The platform connects previously siloed systems while enabling AI use cases in engineering support, outage planning, and sales.
items.title: How Constellation is building a governed data foundation on Databricks

items.summary: Eclipse Aerospace, a light-jet manufacturer and operator, partnered with Databricks to bring nearly two decades of proprietary flight data—totaling more than 3TB across over a million flight hours—into its analytics workflow. Previously the company relied on slow multi-stage pipelines using UDFs, always-on Scala compute, or an AWS Lambda/Avro intermediary that duplicated every file and kept infrastructure running continuously. The new solution uses PySpark custom data sources with a thin Python layer wrapping existing Rust decoders, passing records through Apache Arrow without serialization. This single Spark-native read eliminates network hops, removes duplicate storage (with originals retained in Glacier), improves observability via the Spark UI, and defines schema once.
items.title: Eclipse Aerospace Simplifies Flight-Data Ingestion with Databricks PySpark Custom Data Sources

items.summary: The design of Singapore Airlines' new business class seats has attracted mixed reactions, which the author notes is unsurprising given differing tastes. Rather than focusing on minor features like a narrow yellow strip, attention should go to what matters most: comfortable seating, quality service and overall journey comfort. Cabin designs reflect professional judgment informed by customer feedback, so no design will satisfy everyone; the experience should be judged by the comfort, service and value it delivers.
items.title: Singapore Airlines Business Class Design Draws Mixed Reactions

items.summary: A Bloomberg report suggests Elon Musk's companies could announce a Tesla-SpaceX merger as early as December, potentially the largest ever deal. SpaceX is valued above $1.9 trillion versus Tesla's roughly $1.5 trillion, indicating SpaceX absorbing Tesla rather than vice versa. The transaction would benefit Musk financially through his 2025 CEO award and accelerate 286 million restricted shares from a 2018 package. Governance concerns persist: Musk controls about 85% of SpaceX voting power versus roughly 20% at Tesla, while obstacles include ring-fencing Tesla's China business—where Giga Shanghai shipped over 67,000 vehicles in October—and political scrutiny following midterm shifts.
items.title: SpaceX-Tesla Merger Report and Governance Concerns

items.summary: At the UN's COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, two new reports underscored how far global warming remains from containment. The Climate Action Tracker projects nearly 5 degrees Fahrenheit of warming by 2100, while Copernicus reported that crossing the Paris Agreement's threshold—originally projected around 2045—is now expected as soon as 2029. Analysts say collective government action has stalled for five consecutive years, with fossil fuel expansion undermining progress toward a maximum of 3.4 degrees Fahrenheit by 2100 even under optimistic scenarios.
items.title: COP31 Climate Summit Warns Global Warming Remains Unchecked as Projections Accelerate

items.summary: On November 12, 2026, the Federal Reserve Board announced pricing for payment services it provides to banks and credit unions, effective January 1, 2027. These include check clearing, ACH transactions, instant payments, and wholesale settlement services. The Fed expects to recover 101.5 percent of actual and imputed expenses in 2027, with an estimated average price increase of 1.4 percent for mature services.
items.title: Federal Reserve Board announces pricing, effective January 1, 2027, for payment services the Federal Reserve Banks provide to banks and credit unions, and changes to streamline and adjust their check services

items.summary: Republican and Democratic leaders are coalescing behind new advanced chip export controls on China, which could become law by year's end following the Nvidia scandal involving Jensen Huang. In the House, Speaker Mike Johnson and Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries favor strengthening controls after revelations that Huang had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Senate Majority Leader John Thune cited a 'high probability' of additional restrictions, while Sen. John Kennedy gave it a better-than-even chance. Three measures—the Chip Security Act, MATCH Act, and AI Overwatch Act—could be included in the NDAA, though no final deal exists yet. The scandal has emboldened Congress despite industry opposition.
items.title: Congress Pushes Tighter Chip Export Controls After Nvidia Scandal

items.summary: Bloomberg News reported Thursday that SpaceX and Tesla merger negotiations are progressing, with a deal potentially announced as early as December or slipping into early 2027. The Elon Musk-led companies have discussed both timelines. Neither company could be reached for comment on the report.
items.title: SpaceX, Tesla merger talks progress, Bloomberg News reports

items.summary: According to The Intercept, Russian pranksters Vovan and Lexa impersonated Ukrainian intelligence chief Rustem Umerov on a video call that deceived three senior OpenAI officials for 17 minutes. The conversation touched on providing attack-oriented AI technology to Ukraine amid an ongoing $200 million defense contract with the Pentagon.
items.title: Russian Pranksters Deceived Three OpenAI Executives in a 17-Minute Ukraine AI Call

items.summary: Rumors intensify that Nvidia may replace founder-CEO Jensen Huang amid allegations tied to his personal relationships, including suspicions a woman was a Chinese spy. His prior interview—stating he could be fired and wanted to lead for 20 years—fuels debate as the board convenes; market value fell ~$600 billion in a week.
items.title: Speculation Mounts Over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's Possible Replacement Amid Leadership Uncertainty

items.summary: Exchange Online is Microsoft's cloud-hosted messaging platform, part of the Microsoft 365 suite and the hosted counterpart of on-premises Exchange Server. It stores email plus calendars, contacts and tasks in a single mailbox shared across all devices that sign in, which is why one back-end fault can disrupt every client at once. Because mailboxes are concentrated in this service, outages spread widely; it also underpins Teams' calendar data. Microsoft hosts the servers while customers manage users and settings through admin centers or PowerShell, receiving updates automatically. The article explains how to distinguish local problems from wider service faults using symptom comparison and the health dashboard, then covers MX records, connectors, mail flow rules, Exchange Online Protection, Defender for Office 365 plans, compliance tools, hybrid deployments with Exchange Server, and connection protocols such as MAPI over HTTP, ActiveSync, IMAP, POP, SMTP and Microsoft Graph.
items.title: What Is Exchange Online? The Microsoft Service Behind Outlook Outages

items.summary: Jensen Huang was ousted as Nvidia's CEO Thursday, a dramatic fall for the figure who transformed the company into the centerpiece of the global AI boom. CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim leader while the board searches for a permanent successor; Huang also leaves the board he chaired. His ouster follows revelations about affairs with suspected Chinese spies and subordinates, triggering investigations by Congress, lawmakers, and the DOJ.
items.title: Nvidia Ousts Jensen Huang Amid AI Fallout and Government Scrutiny

items.summary: An editorial argues that the UK's venture capital industry serves foreign investors rather than domestic development, citing a Common Wealth paper. It notes Britain sells valuable startups—DeepMind to Google within four years—before they mature, while pension-fund investment may inflate exit prices without securing ownership. The authors favour democratic control and social-purpose funding, pointing to Brazil, India and Ethiopia as models of homegrown industrial capacity.
items.title: The Guardian editorial on venture capitalism and industrial strategy

items.summary: U.S. existing home sales fell sharply, dropping 8.8% year-over-year to 3.75 million units in October—the weakest performance since 2010 and the lowest level in 16 years—according to the National Association of Realtors. The decline is largely driven by elevated mortgage rates, which peaked at 7.40% for a 30-year fixed loan in October, the highest since 2023. Higher inflation and bond yields have pushed borrowing costs up, while some slowdown was intentional: the Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate in September to curb inflation, with another possible hike in December.
items.title: 'Punch in the gut': U.S. home sales fall to their lowest in 16 years

items.summary: A worldwide Microsoft outage disrupted access to its 365 suite, including Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, OneDrive and Copilot. Down Detector logged nearly 130,000 reports of issues as of the peak before new reports fell. Microsoft said servers were unexpectedly unavailable after configuration updates shifted load onto remaining infrastructure; it paused deployments, restarted affected servers and validated an alternative health check to return them to service.
items.title: Global Microsoft outage disrupts Outlook and Teams

items.summary: Nvidia's board announced that Jensen Huang has resigned as chief executive, with CFO Colette Kress appointed interim boss. The company's shares fell more than 13% when US markets opened after the news but later recovered some ground. BBC North America correspondent Samira Hussain reports on what lies ahead for Nvidia under new leadership.
items.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO; Colette Kress Named Interim Boss

items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Nov. 12, 2026 amid reports of an extramarital relationship with Alice Huang, a Singapore-based executive suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence agencies; he also faced allegations involving another company executive who reports to him. China’s Foreign Ministry denied the espionage claims and accused the U.S. of fabricating spy narratives to justify a technological blockade. The article frames this as a modern instance of an ancient tactic—“meiren ji,” or the beauty stratagem, from China’s Thirty-Six Stratagems—and notes that honey traps are not unique to China, citing Cold War Western and Soviet operations plus cases involving French diplomat Bernard Boursicot and Rep. Eric Swalwell. The author argues Huang’s centrality to U.S.-China AI competition makes him a plausible target, though strategic motive does not prove an operation occurred.
items.title: Has China’s ‘beauty stratagem’ found a new victim in Nvidia’s Jensen Huang?

items.summary: A major Microsoft outage disrupted Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other platforms worldwide. Reports began around 6:25am AEDT, with nearly seven in ten originating from the United States; at its peak over 11,000 reports arrived each minute. Microsoft says some servers are back online while investigating a possible misconfiguration or elevated load.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Affects Teams, Outlook and Copilot Worldwide as Downdetector Charts Global Spread

items.summary: Economists weigh in on Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia as CEO amid an alleged affair with a Chinese spy and company employee. Adam Kobeissi calls it 'a critical mistake' for the industry, warning that much of the AI boom depends on just a few companies like Anthropic, whose IPO may launch soon.
items.title: Nvidia's Exit Under Economic Scrutiny Amid AI Boom Concerns

items.summary: On Thursday, 12 November, a Microsoft services outage disrupted thousands of users worldwide, with the most widespread impact in the Americas. Around 1.30 pm Eastern time (7.30 pm in Italy), more than 120,000 reported Outlook difficulties; this figure rose to over 130,000 per Downdetector data. Microsoft also cited problems with Microsoft 365 and Teams for around 3,000 users. The company attributed the issue to infrastructure overload and began redistributing traffic.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Disrupts Outlook, Teams and Copilot for Thousands of Users

items.summary: The US Coast Guard has suspended a search for a 72-year-old British woman believed to have gone overboard from the Marella Voyager while crossing the Atlantic. Staff noticed her bed untouched on Tuesday; she was last seen around midday Monday, roughly 1,400 nautical miles from Bermuda and about 500 miles from where the report came in. A coordinated international search-and-rescue effort was called off Wednesday due to low survival likelihood, remote location, fuel constraints, sea state and lack of nearby assets.
items.title: Search for British woman missing from Tui cruise ship suspended

items.summary: A study of jaguars (Panthera onca) in the Brazilian Pantanal, based on 13 years of Jaguar ID project surveys since 2013 and citizen science data identifying 459 individuals, found these cats are more social than believed. Of 167 recorded pair interactions, nearly half involved two males, with significant behavioral differences between sexes.
items.title: Jaguars in Brazil's Pantanal Show More Social Behavior Than Expected

items.summary: The China Film Showcase launched in Dublin on November 10, 2026, at the Stella Cinema, drawing more than 200 guests. Attendees included Jiang Haiqing of China Media Group and chairman of CITVC; Zhao Yingguang, chargé d'affaires ad interim of the Chinese Embassy in Ireland; former Irish Prime Minister Enda Kenny; John Kennedy from Ireland's Department of Culture, Communications and Sport; Liang Hong of CMG's Film, Drama and Documentary Center; Danny Byrne; and Anthony Leo of Cartoon Saloon.
items.title: China Film Showcase brings Chinese cinema to Dublin

items.summary: The U.S. government published proposed rules allowing commercial fishing within a Pacific marine reserve exceeding double California's size, covering 1 million square kilometers (408,000 square miles). NOAA Fisheries would permit fishing between 50 and 200 nautical miles from islands including Johnston Atoll, Wake Island, and Jarvis Island. Activists criticize the plan as threatening to culturally significant habitats home to seabirds, sharks, rays, whales, and sea turtles.
items.title: US Proposes Opening Pacific Marine Reserve to Commercial Fishing

items.summary: Latin America faces high logistics costs and inadequate infrastructure that hinder regional development. Chilean historian Renzo Burotto argues that cooperation between China and Latin America can drive infrastructure growth, strengthen multilateralism, and open new opportunities for the Global South. This collaboration is framed as a pathway to address persistent logistical obstacles through shared investment and partnership.
items.title: How Can Latin America Overcome Its Logistics Challenges?

items.summary: Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, prompted by reports of two extramarital affairs, has intensified fears about the future of AI financing. As interim CEO Colette Kress leads the search for a permanent successor, investors reacted sharply: Nvidia shares fell 13%, while rivals Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices advanced. Chinese GPU makers like Moore Threads surged nearly 10% on expectations of market share gains. Huang's exit also raises questions about Nvidia's role as the 'Bank of AI,' having disclosed $164.5 billion in financial commitments, including up to $105 billion tied to an OpenAI data center.
items.title: Nvidia's Leadership Shake-Up Raises Concerns Over AI Financing and Stock Rivalries

items.summary: US stocks fell Friday as a sharp drop in Nvidia outweighed an energy-sector rally, with the S&P 500 down 25.99 points (0.34%) to 7,593.39 and the Nasdaq Composite down 102.44 points (0.40%) to 25,363.75; the Dow fell 190.29 points (0.36%) to 52,296.20. The selloff followed Nvidia naming CFO Colette Kress interim CEO after Jensen Huang's departure and a nearly 18% tumble in Nebius. Despite an earlier intraday plunge of about 12%, Nvidia shares recovered somewhat as rivals like Broadcom, AMD, Alphabet and Amazon provided support.
items.title: US Stocks Close Lower as Nvidia Slide Outweighs Energy Rally

items.summary: Microsoft is investigating connectivity issues affecting Exchange Online mailboxes in the Americas, with over 130,000 reported problems by 1:27 p.m. Eastern time. The outage stems from unexpected server unavailability increasing load rather than user traffic surges. Microsoft 365 and Teams users were also impacted, alongside possibly affected services like SharePoint Online.
items.title: Microsoft Outlook Outage Investigation and Impact Scope

items.summary: US stocks fell Thursday after Nvidia shares plunged nearly 12% following CEO Jensen Huang's departure amid an internal investigation. The S&P 500 dropped 0.34%, Nasdaq lost 0.40%, and the Dow slid 0.36%. Rising oil prices boosted energy stocks, with Brent crude climbing to $95.82 a barrel as higher yields pushed the 10-year Treasury yield above 5%.
items.title: US Stocks Close Lower as Nvidia Slump Overshadows Energy Rally

items.summary: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that former Apple Chief Executive Tim Cook should replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO, calling it a legend replacing a legend. Huang co-founded Nvidia and is its fourth-largest investor; he resigned as CEO and board member after reports of an affair with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of spying for Beijing. CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the company seeks a permanent successor.
items.title: Trump Suggests Tim Cook Replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO

items.summary: A deepening scandal over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's alleged relationship with Alice Huang, whom the board is investigating for allegedly being a Chinese spy, sent Nvidia down 7. 8% premarket toward below $4 trillion market value — its first drop since July 2025 after losing about $300 billion since Sunday's investigation announcement. The selloff dragged AI-linked stocks including neocloud firms CoreWeave (-6%), IREN and Applied Digital, Micron (-3. 4%) and storage makers Sandisk (-5. 1%) and Western Digital (-3. 2%). Rivals AMD (+1. 7%) and Broadcom (+0. 8%) rose on opportunity hopes, while Japan, South Korea and Europe fell roughly 0. 7% to 1%.
items.title: Nvidia rout wipes out $300 billion in market value, drags down AI stocks

items.summary: Anthropic is preparing a US IPO with an indicative price band of $70 to $78 per share and plans to sell 825 million shares, which could raise up to $64.4 billion at the top end. The listing would value the company above $1 trillion under ticker ANT on Nasdaq, targeting November 19 trading start. Anthropic was founded in 2021 by Dario and Daniela Amodei, reported over $16 billion revenue in H1 2026 but remains unprofitable amid heavy AI spending. Indian retail investors face hurdles: while the RBI's Liberalised Remittance Scheme permits overseas investments up to $250,000 annually, IPO allocations typically favor institutions, so most Indians may only buy after listing on Nasdaq.
items.title: Can Indian Investors Apply for Anthropic's $64 Billion IPO?

items.summary: Google is adding its Gemini artificial intelligence app, including hands-free voice mode, to Apple's CarPlay system, Google announced in a blog post Wednesday. Conversations sync to the Gemini iPhone app and work across all supported languages. The feature begins rolling out now globally to iOS users worldwide.
items.title: Google Adds Gemini Voice AI Assistant to Apple CarPlay

items.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath invited CNH Industrial, which is setting up a tractor manufacturing plant in Gautam Buddh Nagar, to also produce bulldozers in the state. Framing this as an opportunity, he argued that UP's reputation for 'bulldozer action' against criminals would automatically generate domestic and international demand. He credited his government's zero-tolerance crime policy with transforming law and order into a business-friendly environment.
items.title: Yogi Adityanath Pushes Bulldozer Manufacturing in Uttar Pradesh

items.summary: At a Deepawali Milan event at BJP headquarters, PM Narendra Modi reflected on the media's transformation from press releases to Instagram reels. He recalled 1990s responsibilities when fax machines were needed for press releases and noted journalists informed him of his Gujarat appointment before party members. Modi marked completing 25 years as head of government.
items.title: PM Modi Recalls Media Evolution from Press Releases to Instagram Reels
